questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard language for creating web pages, defining structure and content.

questions.question: What is the correct HTML5 doctype declaration?
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser this document uses HTML5. It must be the very first line of every HTML document.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used for the main heading of a page?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the main heading. There should be only one per page. Headings go from h1 (most important) to h6 (least important).

questions.question: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?
options: <div> is for images; <span> is for text
questions.explanation: Block-level elements like <div> start on a new line and take full width. Inline elements like <span> flow within text content.

questions.question: Which attribute makes an input field required?
questions.explanation: The 'required' attribute prevents form submission if the field is empty and shows a browser validation message.

questions.question: What does the alt attribute on an tag provide?
options: Alternative text for accessibility and when image fails to load
questions.correct_answer: Alternative text for accessibility and when image fails to load
questions.explanation: alt text is read by screen readers (accessibility) and displayed when the image cannot load. It's required for good HTML practice.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element is used for navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> is a semantic HTML5 element that marks a section containing the main navigation links of a page.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <meta charset='UTF-8'> tag?
options: Adds character count to the page
Specifies the character encoding so browsers correctly display all characters
Sets the language of the page
questions.correct_answer: Specifies the character encoding so browsers correctly display all characters
questions.explanation: UTF-8 supports all Unicode characters including accented letters, emoji, and non-Latin scripts. Always include this in <head>.

questions.question: What is the difference between <article> and <section>?
options: <article> is standalone independent content; <section> groups thematically related content
questions.correct_answer: <article> is standalone independent content; <section> groups thematically related content
questions.explanation: <article> makes sense on its own (blog post, news story). <section> groups related content within a larger context.

questions.question: How do you create an ordered list in HTML?
questions.explanation: <ol> creates a numbered ordered list. <ul> creates a bulleted unordered list. Both use <li> for individual list items.

questions.question: What does the href attribute in <a href='url'> specify?
options: The URL the link navigates to
questions.correct_answer: The URL the link navigates to
questions.explanation: href (Hypertext Reference) specifies the destination URL. Use # for same-page anchor links and mailto: for email links.

questions.question: Which input type shows a date picker in modern browsers?
questions.explanation: type='date' renders a native date picker UI in modern browsers, returning the value in YYYY-MM-DD format.

questions.question: What is the <label> element used for in forms?
options: Associating a text label with a form control for accessibility
questions.correct_answer: Associating a text label with a form control for accessibility
questions.explanation: Clicking a <label> focuses its associated input (via for attribute matching input id). Essential for screen reader accessibility.

questions.question: What does the <head> element contain?
options: Metadata, title, links to CSS/JS — not visible on page
questions.correct_answer: Metadata, title, links to CSS/JS — not visible on page
questions.explanation: <head> contains meta tags, title, charset, favicon, CSS links, and script tags — information about the document, not its content.

questions.question: Which attribute should you use for accessibility on buttons that have no text (icon-only buttons)?
questions.explanation: aria-label provides an accessible name for screen readers when a button has no visible text — critical for icon-only buttons.
